title: Helmet Headset
tagline: A cheap Bluetooth neckband taken apart and rebuilt as a helmet headset
summary: Music, calls and navigation voice in your helmet for about ₹1,800–3,200 instead of a ₹5,000+ communicator, using a cheap Bluetooth neckband's own parts: its board, battery, both speakers and its mic. Its board, battery and buttons go in a slim pod stuck to the outside of the shell on the left with VHB tape (3 big rubber buttons for gloves, sealed, USB-C at the back); the earbuds' own 10 mm speakers go in printed pucks in the liner's ear pockets; its mic goes on a bendable boom held on the helmet's fixed part, so a modular helmet's chin bar flips up over it. No holes in the helmet: the wires go in from below, in the grooves of a flexible cable channel stuck down the shell; besides the neckband, only small hardware bits. General purpose: the helmet's curve and the neckband's parts are settings.
status: Designed and modelled (v1, checked in CAD, not printed or built yet). Designed first for a modular (flip-up) helmet. The neckband (boAt Rockerz 255 Pro+) has no published teardown: open yours and measure its board and battery first.
see_sub: The pod on the left, behind the chin bar's pivot (the helmet is a plain stand-in); inside, the earbuds' speakers in the ear pockets and the neckband's mic on a boom.

gallery.caption: The pod on the left of a modular helmet (a white stand-in), behind the chin bar's pivot: stuck on with VHB tape, no holes
The pod: 102 × 37 mm and 16.5 mm proud of the shell at its middle, 3 rubber domes in a screwed lid, the USB-C plug at its back end, the cables out of its bottom
The cable channel: a flexible TPU strip from the pod's lower edge down to the shell's lower edge; the cables lie in its grooves and go in under the edge trim (no hole in the helmet)
Opened up: the lid, the TPU keypad (also the gasket), the switch board, the neckband's board and the battery
Inside (the stand-in cut open): the left earbud's speaker in its puck in the ear pocket, the neckband's mic on a boom held low on the fixed shell, reaching into the chin bar
The parts that go inside: a speaker puck holding the earbud's own 10 mm speaker, the boom mount and the mic cup
The cable channel as printed, from underneath: a groove for each cable, thin flanges for the tape

docs.label: README: what goes where, the neckband, the pod, wiring, build order

part_groups.label: The pod and its cable channel (outside)

pod_body.name: Pod body
pod_body.what: Holds the neckband's board, its battery and the switch board. Its underside is curved to the shell and stuck on with VHB tape; the USB-C hole at its back end, 2 cable notches at the bottom of its lower wall, right at the shell, lined up with the cable channel; 4 pillars for M2 heat-set inserts
pod_body.material: PETG or ASA, a light colour if you can. Open side down

pod_lid.name: Pod lid
pod_lid.what: Rolled edges, 3 holes for the keypad's domes, ridges between them; 4 M2 × 6 countersunk screws

keypad.name: Keypad
keypad.what: One TPU sheet: its 3 hollow domes are the buttons (the big middle one is play/pause and calls) and its edge is the seam's gasket, squeezed 0.2 mm by the lid

usb_plug.name: USB-C plug
usb_plug.what: Seals the USB-C socket when you ride; pull it out by its tab to charge

speaker_puck.name: Speaker puck
speaker_puck.what: Holds the earbud's own 10 mm speaker (taken out of its shell) at the middle of the liner's ear pocket, with a small closed space behind it; the back is hollowed. Optional 40 mm helmet speakers fit it too (set the speaker size)

mic_cup.name: Mic cup
mic_cup.what: Holds the neckband's own mic on the end of the boom; a foam windscreen goes over it

boom_mount.name: Boom mount
boom_mount.what: A thin plate that slides between the shell and the liner (or sticks to the shell) low on the left, behind the chin bar; the boom pushes into its socket

headset_assembled.name: Pod, assembled
headset_assembled.what: The pod with its keypad, lid and plug

cable_channel.name: Cable channel
cable_channel.what: A flexible strip stuck to the shell from the pod's lower edge down to the shell's lower edge: the 2 cables lie in the grooves on its underside, held flat against the shell, then go in under the edge trim. No hole in the helmet

params.help: Lay a ruler across the spot: radius = L × L / (8 × gap) + gap / 2.
